changes.text: Avoid a fail-back (on by default): with override disabled, a rejoining unit with the higher HA priority takes the primary role back if the other unit has been up for less than ha-uptime-diff-margin (300 s by default), causing a second failover. The app reads the margin, override and priorities, times how long the upgraded unit took to come back, and holds the cutover until it will be older than the margin when the old primary rejoins.

No wait when the upgraded unit has the higher priority; with override on, the app explains that priority always decides instead of waiting. After the old primary rejoins, the log says which unit is primary and flags a fail-back if one happened.
Wizard option under Service-gated, and an Avoid fail-back stage in the diagram with a countdown. Stop waiting carries on and marks the stage.

title: Record HA status when rejoin is unconfirmed

changes.text: If a service-gated upgrade can't confirm the upgraded unit is back in the cluster after 2 minutes, it records 'get system ha status' from the cluster address and from that unit (over SSH) in the job log, so it is clear afterwards whether the unit was a secondary, alone, or a second primary.

Service-gated rejoin stopped at the first source that answered. A 7.6.8 primary's HA peer list can leave out a peer that runs 8.0.2, so the upgraded unit looked absent. The check now also asks the upgraded unit itself and 'get system ha status' over SSH, and only waits on when none of them shows the unit back with all units.
When the unit isn't seen back after 15 minutes, the question explains the risk: if it isn't a secondary, upgrading the primary next takes the whole cluster down while it reboots.

Service-gated upgrades waited up to 30 minutes after the first unit was upgraded: while the units run different firmware, the primary answers ha-checksums with HTTP 500, which the rejoin check took as 'not back yet'. Rejoin is now read from the HA peer list (then HA statistics, then checksums) on the cluster address, then on the upgraded unit's own address, then from 'get system ha status' over SSH.
Each rejoin check is logged with what it saw (e.g. '1 of 2 units in the cluster (cluster address, ha-peer)'), and after 15 minutes the upgrade asks whether to carry on instead of waiting silently.

title: Upgrades no longer hang after the image is sent

changes.text: An upgrade could stay on Transfer image for up to 30 minutes: an HA primary can accept the image and go straight on to upgrading the cluster without ever answering the upload request. The request now runs in the background; once the image has been sent, the app checks the device every 10 s, and a unit that stops answering because it is rebooting, a unit that left the cluster, or a unit reporting the new version counts as the install having started. The same applies to FortiGuard downloads.

Transfer image shows the upload progress (percent and MB sent), then how long it has been waiting for the FortiGate to accept the image. Stop waiting lets you continue; the reboot wait still confirms the new version. If the device neither answers nor starts installing within 15 minutes, the upgrade stops with a clear message.

SSH logins to an HA unit timed out although they had reached the prompt: FortiOS shows the HA role in the prompt (fgt-vm04-a(Primary) #), which wasn't recognised. CLI checks, configuration reads over SSH and reading the other unit's address work again on clusters.

New FGCP upgrade mode, Service-gated (FortiOS 7.4.1+): the app sets upgrade-mode local-only and upgrades one unit at a time through each unit's own address. Each secondary must be back on the new firmware and in the cluster, and every service probe must have had no failures for a set time (default 60 s), before the primary is upgraded. The primary's reboot is the cutover, so it only happens once services are stable.

Options for the gate: how long services must be stable, how long to wait before asking you (default 15 min), and an optional go-ahead before the cutover. After the last unit the cluster must be in sync and the services stable again; the HA setting is then restored.
The stage diagram shows each unit's transfer, install and rejoin, the service gates with what they are waiting for, and the cutover approval. Stop waiting works on the gates too.
An approval asked part-way through an upgrade is shown on the stage that asked, not on the earlier Go-ahead stage.

An FGCP hop is only complete when every unit runs the new firmware. The cluster address answers on the new version as soon as an upgraded unit takes over, while the old primary is still installing; each unit with a saved address is now checked through its own address (new stage: Every unit upgraded).
HA in sync requires every unit to be back in the cluster with matching checksums, recognises FortiOS 7.4+/8.0's primary flag, and shows how many units are in the cluster and in sync while it waits.

Service monitoring after the upgrade waits until every probe has been stable (no failures) for 20 s, instead of up at one instant, so a target that drops for a second every few seconds no longer keeps it waiting for the full 5 minutes without saying why. The stage names the unstable probes and the time left.

Stop waiting: while an upgrade is only waiting to confirm a result (every unit on the new firmware, HA sync, services stable), the install view says what it is waiting for and lets you stop the wait. The step is marked for attention and the upgrade carries on. Installs and reboots are never cut short.

The install view shows each device's upgrade as a diagram above the log: one row per phase (Prepare, each firmware hop, Finish), each stage a node on a line, coloured by status (pending, in progress, waiting for approval, done, skipped, failed), with how long it took.

Stages are planned from the actual upgrade: connect and plan, pre-checks, go-ahead, set HA upgrade mode, then per hop transfer image, install and reboot, and HA in sync, then restore HA setting, post-checks and compare. FGSP rolling upgrades show each peer.

Live notes on each stage: the upgrade path, the reboot progress (elapsed time, still running the old version, back on the new build), the HA sync state, the HA setting changed, and the pre/post difference counts. A failed stage shows the error.
Jobs › an upgrade's details show the same diagram, and it is kept with the job history.
Create New opens a guided Add device: enter any management address and the API token, and the app connects (read-only) and detects whether it is a standalone unit, an FGCP cluster or an FGSP peer.

For an FGCP cluster it recognises whether the address is the shared cluster address or one unit's own address (management-ip or dedicated HA management interface), lists every unit with its role, priority and serial, suggests the cluster address, and fills in each unit's own address (the other unit's read over SSH when SSH credentials are given).

Check addresses confirms the cluster address reaches the primary and each unit address reaches that unit (by serial number). The device can't be saved until the cluster address checks out; missing or failed unit addresses ask for confirmation.
Enter details manually keeps the token and SSH password typed in the guided form.

title: Every HA unit on the dashboard

changes.text: An HA cluster's dashboard reads every unit through its own address (its saved unit address, management-ip or dedicated HA management interface) and shows each unit's hostname, serial number, model, VM series, firmware, licences, resources, interfaces and ports, not just the unit that was polled.

Cluster units table: role, HA priority, serial, model, firmware, CPU, memory, sessions, FortiCare and address for every unit side by side, with a warning when the units run different firmware. Pick a unit to see its full details.

A unit with no saved address is read through the own address found from the primary (over SSH), using the device's API token, which HA keeps the same on every unit. A unit that can't be reached is still listed from what the primary reports, with what to add.
The HA cluster panel shows each unit's real port link state when that unit can be read.
Edit a device and click Show next to REST API token to see the saved token, with a Copy button. It hides again after a minute; the token is never written to logs.

New upgrade wizard step, Config & log review, before pre-flight. It reads each unit's configuration, HA settings, licences, resources and recent event logs (read-only) and lists what could make an HA upgrade fail or cause problems afterwards, with what to do about each.

Licensing: security profiles used by enabled policies without a valid licence (antivirus, IPS, web/DNS/video filter, application control, antispam), licences about to expire, no FortiCare contract (critical for FortiGuard downloads) and invalid VM licences.
Removed or changed features in the target version (from the built-in and your own rules), and compatibility of FortiAnalyzer, FortiManager, managed FortiSwitch/FortiAP/FortiExtender and EMS.

HA: cluster out of sync (which checksums differ), single unit in the cluster, mixed models, session pickup off, override on (extra failover), single heartbeat link, no monitored interfaces, monitored interface set down, no per-unit management address.

Logs: recent event logs grouped into problem patterns (conserve mode, crashes, HA sync and heartbeat loss, hardware, disk, interface flapping, routing, VPN, SD-WAN, FortiGuard, configuration errors, failed admin logins) with counts, time range and the latest events. Over SSH it also reads the crash log and the configuration lines FortiOS rejected at the last boot.
Critical findings must be acknowledged before continuing. The review is included in the PDF upgrade report.
Configuration and before/after diffs have a Maximise button that fills the window (Esc restores it), so long lines don't wrap or get cut off.
A− / A+ font-size controls (9-20 px) on both diff views; the size is remembered.
Snapshots & Diff lists every collection of every device and sorts by date, hostname, device, collection or firmware (click a column heading), with device, collection-type and text filters.

Opening a collection shows it side by side with its partner (an upgrade's before and after collections, otherwise the next collection of the same unit), with changed lines and the changed part of each line highlighted. Changes only or the full file, previous/next change, and before/after pickers.

A delta summary tile at the top of the comparison: firmware, critical/warning/informational counts, configuration settings changed, and a table of every check's before and after value. Click a row to jump to that section.
The dashboard shows the data folder in its own tile with an Open button.
The dashboard's device type counts include units saved as Standalone that report FGCP or FGSP HA.
First release published on GitHub with a macOS disk image and a Windows installer. It includes everything in v0.11.0: in-app update checks, verified downloads and self-install.
The release build's tests now allow for the 1-second minimum HTTP probe interval, so builds no longer fail by chance.
Ready-built downloads on GitHub Releases: a macOS disk image (.dmg) and a Windows installer (Setup .exe), with SHA-256 checksums.
The app checks GitHub for a newer release at start-up and every 6 hours, and offers to download and install it. The download is verified against the release checksum before installing.
Installing an update closes the app, replaces it (macOS) or runs the installer silently (Windows), and reopens it.
Settings › Software updates: installed and latest version, Check now, and a switch for automatic checks. An update badge appears under the version at the bottom left.
Release builds for macOS and Windows are produced by a GitHub Actions workflow when a version tag is pushed.
The software version and build are shown at the bottom left of the window, as on FortiOS. Click it to open the change log.
System > Change log lists every release with its build, date and changes.
The macOS app bundle and the PDF report carry the version and build.
The app has its own icon (firewall shield with an upgrade arrow) instead of the Python logo, for macOS (.icns) and Windows (.ico).

title: Per-unit HA addresses for service probes

changes.text: Default probes for an HA cluster target each unit's own management-ip or dedicated HA management interface, never the shared cluster address, so each unit's availability is shown separately.
A secondary's own address is read from the primary over SSH (execute ha manage, then show system interface) when it isn't saved on the device.
The HA cluster panel shows each unit's own address and fills it into Save addresses.

title: HA cluster view and upgrade hardening

changes.text: HA dashboard shows both units as appliances with the heartbeat link, role, HA priority, serial and cluster settings.
Save addresses re-saves a cluster as cluster address plus unit addresses, reusing its API token and SSH login.
The upgrade wizard adds probes for every management address automatically, respecting each interface's allowed access and the admin HTTPS port.
Temporary connection errors (TLS handshake refused, connection reset) on read-only API calls are retried twice instead of failing the upgrade.
An SSH login that stops at a password-change or disclaimer screen fails within seconds with a clear message, instead of hanging for 100 seconds.
HTTP(S) probes run at most once a second (default every 2 s), so they can't overload the FortiGate's management web server.

title: HA mode choice and dashboard layout

changes.text: A unit saved as Standalone that reports FGCP or FGSP is upgraded as a cluster, and the wizard asks for its HA upgrade and failover mode.
The wizard, device form and README explain the cluster address and per-unit HA management addresses.
Dashboard panels size to their content; text wraps instead of running past panel edges.
Rapid ping, TCP connect and HTTP(S) probes run during an upgrade and measure each outage window, tagged with the upgrade step that caused it.
Live timeline on the Install page, kept in the upgrade history and the PDF report.
The dashboard shows a FortiGate-VM's series (VM01, VM02, VM04 ... VMUL), licence type and vCPU/RAM allowance.

title: PDF report and FortiOS 8.0 backup fixes

changes.text: Server errors are logged and shown with their real message; the report retries from the saved job.
FortiOS 8.0's refusal of unencrypted backups is detected instead of being stored as configuration; the configuration is read over SSH instead.
The macOS build is swapped in atomically and warns when the app is running.
The wizard's final screen generates a PDF report: settings, pre-flight, per-device timeline, pre/post checks, diffs, warnings, errors and the activity log.
Local images are uploaded as a file (like the FortiOS GUI), avoiding HTTP 413; base64 is the fallback.
A failed upgrade shows the stage it failed in.
Device Configuration tab: view any saved configuration, diff two past configurations, or diff the current one against a chosen earlier one.
Firmware images are matched by model code, so FortiGate-VM and FortiFirewall images are recognised for the right devices.
Step-by-step upgrade wizard showing the target image and install method throughout, with Next buttons and warnings instead of typing UPGRADE.
Verbose live log in a terminal-style window, including every API and SSH call.
The dashboard draws each model's front panel with its physical ports only (no NPU links).
Secrets live in one encrypted vault with a single keychain item (or a local key file), ending repeated keychain prompts.
Per-device dashboard with tabs: system information, current status with compare, known issues, upgrade history and current jobs.
FortiOS-style look; the app is renamed FortiGate Upgrader.

Upgrades standalone FortiGates, FGCP and FGSP clusters over the REST API, with pre/post checks and diffs, upgrade path validation, FortiGuard download or local image push, HA upgrade modes, batch upgrades, a firmware store and FortiManager detection.
